The term artificial intelligence (AI) was coined and effectively popularized by American computer scientist John McCarthy.
While others like Alan Turing had previously worked on the concept of "thinking machines," McCarthy gave the field its enduring name and formal identity.
He coined it in his workshop proposal in 1955 for an academic conference. He felt other terms in use, like "cybernetics" or "automata theory," were too restrictive.
